reading.body:
Jennifer Kiggans's AI record is legislative and financial at once: four AI bills sponsored or cosponsored, four recorded votes, and seven committee contributions from Amazon, Google, and Intel PACs.

The contributions are small and repeated rather than large and singular. Google's PAC gives $2,000 in March 2025, $2,000 in June 2025, and $1,000 twice on the same day in July 2026. Amazon gives $2,000 in June 2025 and $1,000 in August 2026. Intel gives $2,000 in November 2025. The pattern is routine PAC giving to a member, not a single decisive transfer.

The legislative side runs in the same window. She cosponsored the CREATE AI Act in March 2025, sponsored the AI for America Act in November 2025, and cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act in December 2025 and the Deterring American AI Model Theft Act in April 2026. The bills span research funding, export controls, and model theft, which are different parts of AI policy rather than one theme.

What the data does not show is causation, and the page says so. Contributions and bill positions are listed in date order only. There is no vote count on the sponsored bills, no committee assignment, no district data on data centers or power, and no indication of whether any contribution preceded, followed, or influenced any legislative act. For AI specifically, the record shows a member engaged on export and model-security questions, which sit closer to compute access and chip policy than to the grid.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Jennifer Kiggans: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 15 events.
